title.narrative: Strengthening National Capacity for SEA Investigations in Mozambique

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project aims to strengthen Mozambique’s national capacity to prevent, respond to, and investigate Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) by equipping national NGOs and institutions with survivor centred investigative competencies, robust safeguarding systems, harmonized PSEA communication materials, and an updated, context specific SEA risk analysis. Although reporting pathways have improved, the 2023 Inter Agency SEA Risk Assessment revealed persistent gaps in investigative skills, due process, safeguarding practices, and consistent application of survivor centred standards across national partners. National NGOs continue to face challenges in managing SEA allegations safely, ethically, impartially, and in alignment with Mozambican legislation and global standards. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTo address these gaps, the project provides structured leadership training, specialized investigation training, contextualized tools and guidance, and post training mentorship from qualified investigation experts. These efforts will establish a stronger national foundation for safe SEA case management and contribute to a sustainable, inter agency pool of trained Mozambican investigators. A core pillar of the project is the institutionalization of a victim /survivor centred approach (VCA), as required under the UN Protocol on the Provision of Assistance to Victims of SEA, reinforcing key principles including safety, dignity, confidentiality, informed consent/assent, non discrimination, and Do No Harm, and ensuring timely referral to appropriate GBV and Child Protection services.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project acknowledges the essential role of women led organizations, which frequently act as first responders and trusted entry points for SEA and GBV disclosures, particularly for women and girls, and the heightened vulnerability of persons with disabilities, who face increased risk of sexual exploitation and abuse and greater barriers to reporting and accessing assistance. By engaging women led organizations and integrating disability perspectives within capacity strengthening and system level activities, the project enhances the inclusivity, relevance, and effectiveness of national PSEA mechanisms.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project also integrates global best practices from the IASC Investigators’ Manual, emphasising trauma informed interviewing, effective rapport building, risk assessments, evidence based investigation planning, and measures to prevent re traumatization and retaliation.Complementing the investigative component, harmonized PSEA communication materials will strengthen prevention efforts and improve community facing clarity, while an updated national SEA risk analysis will enable partners to more effectively anticipate, mitigate, and monitor protection risks. Collectively, these interventions will contribute to a more coherent, accountable, and survivor centred national PSEA system anchored within the Mozambique PSEA Network.ltbrgtlt/pgt
